_comment: How the spec's Einsum labels map onto the IR, and the few facts the IR
does not carry.
labels: written Einsum -> position in the IR cascade, in running order. A
LIST means one written Einsum lowered to several IR nodes; E04 is a
three-arm `cases` whose arms run in order, each overwriting the last,
which is what makes the u=s arm win. The reader wrote one Einsum, so the
trace shows one step.
Which of these run once and which run every generation is DERIVED, not
listed: an Einsum whose output generation is a rank variable carries the
generational rank and belongs to the loop; one writing a fixed generation
does not. The loop belongs to the rank, not to a marked begin and end.
The stopping condition is checked after each completed generation -- a
do-while -- with the rank bound to the generation just finished, so a
predicate over i+1 reads what that generation produced.
selectors: a populate's COORDINATE op -> the rule this run uses. The
coordinate op is the one that chooses; compute_op only says what value to
write once a coordinate is chosen. An unmapped name stops the cascade
rather than being guessed at.
select-one-admissible-v is genuinely free: E10 is written
1(pick-admissible-edge), which says ANY admissible edge. So the default is
seeded-random, not a rule -- a deterministic rule would make the spec
claim something it does not, and would sample the legal executions with a
bias. Seeded so a build is reproducible.
displayNames: tensors the spec names one way and the write-up another. The
interpreter aliases on read; the driver aliases on write too, or Delta and
delta become two tensors that never meet.
